    "failure_scenario": "`return sum(values)` does the same job, has no start-index to get wrong, and gives the correct result for empty and one-element lists. The hand-written `result = 0; for i in range(...)` form adds maintenance cost and already produced the bug above."

The range `7c93e38..HEAD` covers only `stats.py` (commit c3). There is also a bug in `loop.py`, outside the range, from commit c2. In `first_negative_index`, `i` is never incremented, so any list whose first element is non-negative loops forever. I did not include it in the findings because it is out of scope.
